items.title: Add the degree, then the other side

states.label: A quality
states.note: The quality word has its ordinary shape.

states.label: A higher degree
states.note: *Atu* carries the comparative degree. The quality word keeps its shape.

states.label: The other side named
states.sm: E malosi atu le tama i lo le teine.
states.en: The boy is stronger than the girl.
states.note: The phrase with *i lo* comes last and names what the boy is compared with.

items.caption: Step through the printed sentences. Degree and the other side of the comparison arrive as separate words.

items.title: Likeness or agreement?

prompts.sm: Sā tautala le tama e pei sā i ai.
prompts.why: *Pei* can compare with an imagined situation: as if he had been there.

prompts.sm: E tautala le tama e pei o se saienitisi.
prompts.why: *Pei* likens the way the boy talks to a scientist.

prompts.sm: Sā siva le teine e tusa ma le finagalo o le tamā.
prompts.why: *Tusa ma* says that the dancing is in accordance with the wish.
